Get Comparison Parameter Information

Source: R/f_comparison_parameters.R
getComparisonParameterInfo.Rd

Describes the observed values and plotting roles of comparison-data columns. This analysis does not change, round, or recalculate the supplied data.

Usage

getComparisonParameterInfo(
  data,
  ...,
  removeConstantParameters = FALSE,
  binaryIntegerAsFactor = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame, typically returned by getComparisonData(). Columns must be one-dimensional atomic vectors, including factors and dates.

...

Further arguments. Currently unused.

removeConstantParameters

Whether to omit columns with at most one distinct observed value. Defaults to FALSE so all parameters are available.

binaryIntegerAsFactor

Whether integer-valued binary variables are also eligible for use as factors. This does not change the source column.

Value

A data.frame with one row per column: paramName, dataType, paramType, isContinuous, isFactor, isBinary, isEmpty, isSingleValue, isConstant, isVarying, hasMissingValues, paramLevelLength, and binaryValues (display text). The list columns values and singleValue preserve the original value types and precision; singleValue contains NULL except for single-valued columns. Empty inputs produce a zero-row table with the same schema.

Details

Missing values and blank character/factor entries are excluded from observed levels. They are recorded in hasMissingValues. Thus a column containing one value and NA is constant among observed values; it is not identical to a complete column. Empty columns are constant but are not single-valued. Numeric character columns are recognized when every observed entry is a signed decimal or scientific numeric literal, or a comma-separated sequence of these literals as exported for vector-valued parameters. Every token must be numeric; incomplete or mixed text sequences remain character. Original cell values are retained without parsing them as R code. dataType records the original first class; paramType records the inferred plotting type. Finite, exactly integral numeric values are classified as integer without integer coercion. Factors and date/time classes retain their types. isFactor describes eligibility for categorical use, rather than whether the original column is an R factor. isContinuous and isFactor may both be TRUE for integer-valued binary data.

Variation is evaluated across rows, including stages and situations. This is not a test of differences between complete stage profiles of separate objects. No numerical tolerance is applied to distinctness. Unused factor levels do not count as observed values.

Examples

data <- data.frame(alpha = c(0.025, 0.025), effect = c(0.2, 0.3))
getComparisonParameterInfo(data)
#>   paramName dataType paramType isContinuous isFactor isBinary isEmpty
#> 1     alpha  numeric   numeric         TRUE    FALSE    FALSE   FALSE
#> 2    effect  numeric   numeric         TRUE    FALSE     TRUE   FALSE
#>   isSingleValue isConstant isVarying hasMissingValues paramLevelLength
#> 1          TRUE       TRUE     FALSE            FALSE                1
#> 2         FALSE      FALSE      TRUE            FALSE                2
#>   binaryValues   values singleValue
#> 1         <NA>    0.025       0.025
#> 2     0.2, 0.3 0.2, 0.3        NULL
